# CrazyCauldron Roadmap

## How to read this roadmap

This is where CrazyCauldron and COOK go after launch. It is a plan, not a promise: the order and timing can change, and how much we build depends on how many people play. We are funding development ourselves and will keep investing time and money as the game grows.

Items move from Later to Next as more players join. COOK is a community token; nothing here is financial advice, and we make no promises about its price or about any rewards.

## Next after launch

| Item | What it means for you | We start when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| More room for players | More servers, so a room is open when you want to play | The game regularly fills; launch capacity is about 300 players at once |
| Smoother updates | Updates that keep you connected instead of restarting the game | After the first launch update |
| Art overhaul | Redrawn characters with full outfits, matching the painted world | Once launch has settled |
| Seasons | Each season adds one new cooking technique (smoking, fermenting or baking) and raises the skill level cap from 20 toward 50 | Once launch has settled |

## Later, if the game grows

| Item | What it means for you |
| --- | --- |
| More skills and zones | Hunting, plus expeditions to deeper zones with rarer ingredients |
| Legendary dishes and mastery | A top quality tier, bonuses for dishes you cook often, and a permanent credit for the first player to discover a recipe |
| Feasts | Multi-course dishes that give a buff to everyone visiting your camp |
| Weekly Chef's Challenge | A weekly cook-off ranked by dish score, with titles and plates as prizes |
| Cosmetics and community votes | More cosmetics, camp decorations and name changes you can buy with COOK at fixed prices (half of every purchase is burned), and seasonal votes by COOK holders on themes; power always comes from cooking skill, never from a token balance |
| Holder tiers | Holding more COOK unlocks extra cosmetics, a bigger offline cooking pot and a holder-only area; cosmetics and convenience only, never cooking power |
| Pay upgrades in coins or COOK | Pan and bag upgrades can be bought with either in-game coins or COOK, your choice; COOK spent this way is half burned |
| Player market | Sell your coins and dishes to other players for COOK on an in-game market, with a small treasury fee; planned only if the player base is healthy, with anti-bot rules in place first |
